frequency_question: How often does a wildly outlying, highly contested major regulatory fee increase successfully reach final publication in the Federal Register within a single presidential year window?
membership_rule: Includes major federal agency rulemakings proposing fee increases exceeding 500% of baseline or establishing absolute fee levels far above historical norms that faced immediate judicial or stakeholder threats of blockage. Excludes routine annual adjustments or minor fee modifications.

cases.name: USCIS Premium Processing Fee Major Structural Adjustments (2020)
DHS Public Charge Rule Fee and Affidavit Adjustments (2019)
FCC Restoring Internet Freedom Order Regulatory Fee Schedules (2018)

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.3x)
coverage_note: 3 named; believed roughly 4 comparable major outlier fee rulemakings in recent decades.
known_gaps: Excludes minor fee schedules and rules finalized under emergency declarations without standard notice-and-comment.
skeleton: Three major regulatory fee or immigration-related structural overhaul cycles involving high friction and extreme cost jumps since 2017, each resulting in published final rules despite litigation.
multiplier: 3 observed major contested fee/structural rule finalizations divided by 4 attempted comparable high-salience outlier rules = 75%
validity_reason: Base rate tied directly to the current presidential administration's rulemaking velocity and litigative posture, which resets at the end of the presidential term.
